issues.legal_issue: Land that has vested absolutely in the State before a later change in the applicable acquisition law is not divested, and a delayed award does not cause the acquisition to lapse.
material_facts: The acquisition notice was published and the land vested absolutely in the State, free from encumbrances, before the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 was extended to the State.
The awards were made after the period that the appellants said applied under the Land Acquisition Act.
The appellants challenged the acquisitions on the grounds that the later extension of the Land Acquisition Act displaced the earlier proceedings and that the awards were untimely.
issues.conclusion: The later extension of the Land Acquisition Act and subsequent amendments did not divest land already vested in the State. The two-year award requirement in Section 11-A did not apply to undo the completed vesting, and the acquisitions did not lapse even if the awards were delayed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 52(4) of the Rajasthan Urban Improvement Act, publication of the acquisition notice vests the land absolutely in the State, free from encumbrances. Such completed vesting is analogous to vesting following possession under Section 17(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894. Applying Satendra Prasad Jain v. State of U.P., P. Chinnanna v. State of A.P., and Awadh Bihari Yadav v. State of Bihar, once land has vested under the urgent-acquisition provision, Section 11-A does not cause the acquisition to lapse for failure to make an award within its prescribed period, and the State cannot withdraw from the acquisition under Section 48.

predicates.acquisition_challenge_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal challenging the validity of a land acquisition.
predicates.land_vested_before_later_law_applied: The land vested absolutely in the acquiring government before a later change in the applicable acquisition law took effect.
predicates.award_delayed: The award was made later than the period asserted to govern the acquisition.

issues.definition: When an acquisition challenge appeal concerns land that vested before a later change in law and the award was delayed, the acquisition does not lapse.

issues.legal_issue: Land may be acquired for improvement or another purpose under the applicable urban-improvement law without a scheme having been framed or finalized.
material_facts: The land was acquired for improvement of an urban area, including construction of residential, commercial, and industrial buildings.
The appellants relied on a High Court decision to argue that acquisition could not proceed without a sanctioned scheme and that the proposed use had to conform to the Master Plan.

The Supreme Court relied on its earlier decision concerning the same urban-improvement law, which held that a scheme is mandatory when the Trust undertakes the work, but not when the State Government or one of its departments undertakes development.
issues.conclusion: A scheme need not be framed or finalized for the State Government to acquire land under the Act for improvement or another purpose under the Act; the acquisition was not invalid for want of a scheme.
issues.legal_principle: Section 52(1) of the Rajasthan Urban Improvement Act authorizes acquisition when the State Government considers land necessary for improvement or another purpose under the Act. Gandhi Grah Nirman Sahkari Samiti Ltd. v. State of Rajasthan holds that a scheme is mandatory when the Trust undertakes the work, but the State Government may undertake development without a scheme under Chapter V. The Court also held that the Division Bench decision in Narain v. State of Rajasthan did not state the correct law and had been disapproved by the High Court Full Bench.

predicates.acquisition_challenge_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal challenging the validity of a land acquisition.
predicates.acquisition_for_urban_improvement_or_oth: The government acquired the land for urban improvement or another purpose authorized by the applicable law.
predicates.no_scheme_framed: No scheme for the proposed work had been framed or finalized.

issues.definition: When an acquisition challenge appeal concerns land acquired for an authorized urban-improvement purpose without a framed scheme, the acquisition may be valid without a scheme.

issues.legal_issue: Failure to comply with transitional requirements concerning an award or payment does not undo vesting that occurred before the transitional provisions took effect.
material_facts: The land had vested in the State before the commencement of the validating legislation that introduced transitional provisions for pending acquisitions.
The awards and payments were made within the periods specified by the transitional provisions, according to the Court.
The Court held that even non-compliance with those transitional requirements would not affect vesting that had already occurred.
issues.conclusion: The transitional provisions did not undo the prior vesting; non-compliance with their requirements concerning the award or payment would not divest the land or cause the acquisition to lapse.
issues.legal_principle: Section 60-A(1) of the Rajasthan Urban Improvement Act preserved actions already taken under the earlier law, while Section 60-A(3) and (4) set transitional requirements concerning awards and payment. The Court treated the payment provision as analogous to Section 17(3-A) of the Land Acquisition Act and, applying Satendra Prasad Jain v. State of U.P., P. Chinnanna v. State of A.P., and Awadh Bihari Yadav v. State of Bihar, held that failure to meet such a requirement does not undo completed vesting.

predicates.acquisition_challenge_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal challenging the validity of a land acquisition.
predicates.land_vested_before_transitional_requirem: The land vested in the acquiring government before new transitional requirements for pending acquisitions took effect.
predicates.transitional_award_or_payment_requiremen: A requirement concerning the award or payment under the transitional arrangements was not met.

issues.definition: When an acquisition challenge appeal concerns land that vested before transitional requirements took effect, failure to meet an award or payment requirement does not undo that vesting.
